subject: Proposal: eval runner + API schema enforcement for Meridian POC
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: dev.patel@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, camila.reyes@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 26 Sep 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Proposal: eval runner + API schema enforcement for Meridian POC

Team —

Quick context: Meridian (contact: Aisha Patel) is close to committing on a Dedicated contract but has pushed a hard requirement: they want an automated eval runner + strict API schema enforcement that will (a) run our eval suite against their prompt set nightly during the POC, and (b) block any model rollout that changes structured output fields used by their downstream pipeline. They made this a gating item in procurement.

As discussed with Marissa/Ben, this is a high-dollar deal (see HubSpot link below) and the customer timeline is tight — they want the nightly evals and schema checks running against a sample of traffic by Oct 6 to validate performance and regressions before signing.

Ask: can Eng/Product prioritize a lightweight eval-runner (runner + a simple schema-enforcement hook) for the next sprint (two-week window)? We're not asking for a full platform integration — MVP can be cron-driven runner that posts results to shared Drive and a pre-deploy schema check that returns a non-blocking warning first, then we flip to blocking after 1 week if stable.

Attached: Meridian_Eval_Specs_v1.pdf (evaluation cases + success criteria), POC-success-criteria.xlsx, sync notes. HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deals/12345

Impact if we do this: much higher chance to close this deal this quarter and we get a concrete customer-driven use case for automated evals + SLOs that we can productize later.

If this needs an SLA exception or dedicated cycles, please call it out. I'm happy to take the ask to leadership if we need to reallocate.

Next steps: Dev/Hannah — can we scope a minimal implementation and estimate? Marissa/Ben — I'll surface the tradeoffs to Meridian and confirm acceptance criteria.

— Jordan
Jordan Blake
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
From: Dev Patel <dev.patel@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: hannah.schmitt@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 28 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: eval runner + API schema enforcement for Meridian POC

Jordan —

Thanks for the context. A few quick clarifying questions so we scope correctly:

1) What does Meridian expect the nightly runner to execute? Full regen of a 500-prompt eval set with embeddings + reranking + structured-field checks, or a subset (e.g., 50 critical prompts)?
2) Schema enforcement: do they want pre-deploy blocking on any schema mismatch, or only field-level presence/typing checks? Any examples from their pipeline we can use?
3) Runtime environment: do they expect this to run in their VPC (private) or can we run it in hosted with sample payloads? If it's in their VPC we need security sign-off and possibly infra time.

Technical note: a minimal runner that exercises model inference + a schema validator (jsonschema-based) is feasible in ~5 dev-days if we limit to a 100-prompt set and hosted execution. If we need to support pre-deploy enforcement integrated with our rollout system, that's additional work (est. +6 dev-days) to add the gating hook.

I'll start a quick spike tomorrow to wire a basic runner (script + config) if Hannah gives the green light.

— Dev
From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, dev.patel@redwood.com
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 29 Sep 2026 11:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: eval runner + API schema enforcement for Meridian POC

Thanks for the clear ask, Jordan. I pulled this into product triage this morning. High level thoughts:

- Business priority: I agree this is important and could unlock the deal. We need a clear acceptance criteria doc from Meridian (Aisha) stating what constitutes a pass/fail for the nightly run and which fields are critical.
- Scope recommendation (MVP):
  * Eval runner: host a lightweight job that runs a configurable subset (default 100 prompts) nightly and uploads results to the shared Drive + a simple HTML dashboard.
  * Schema enforcement: JSON schema validation for structured outputs with a configurable failure threshold (e.g., 5% failures => block rollout). Start with presence/type checks only.
- Risks: Integrating the gating into our rollout automation and adding blocking rules affects canary deploys. I'd prefer we ship non-blocking warnings in sprint 1 and enable blocking after a successful week of runs.
- Resource ask: We can commit 1.5 sprints of Eng effort (Dev + 0.5 for infra) if Sales can confirm the customer will sign a timeboxed commitment on expansion within 60 days of POC success.

Jordan/Marissa: please confirm whether Meridian will accept the staged approach (warnings -> blocking) and the 60-day expansion commitment. If yes, we'll slot this as a sprint priority.

— Hannah
Product Manager | Redwood Inference
From: Aisha Patel <aisha@meridian.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: ravi.singh@meridian.ai, procurement@meridian.ai
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 08:22:00 -04:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: eval runner + API schema enforcement for Meridian POC

Jordan / Marissa —

Thanks for moving quickly on this. Meridian can accept the staged approach you described (non-blocking warnings for the first week, then blocking after we jointly validate stability). We will commit to a 60-day expansion conversation following successful POC results.

For the nightly runner, we will start with a focused set of 120 prompts that exercise our top 5 API output fields. I've attached an internal mapping file (shared via Drive link) and flagged the two fields that are most critical for our downstream processing.

We need the runner in place and the first nightly run completed by Oct 6 to keep the procurement timeline. Please let us know what data format you need for the prompts and sample payloads.

Best,
Aisha Patel
Director of ML Platform, Meridian AI
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
To: dev.patel@redwood.com, hannah.schmitt@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: ben.carter@redwood.com, camila.reyes@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 01 Oct 2026 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposal: eval runner + API schema enforcement for Meridian POC — alignment and next steps

Team — quick summary and requests:

1) Customer (Meridian) confirmed staged approach and 60-day post-POC expansion commitment (see Aisha's note). They need the first nightly run by Oct 6.
2) Dev: please proceed with the minimal runner spike (100-120 prompts) in hosted mode and wire in a jsonschema-based validator for the top two critical fields. Keep the gating non-blocking initially. Estimate and blockers due EOD tomorrow.
3) Hannah: please create a short runbook for the POC operator (how to trigger runs, where results land, how to flip blocking on). Put it in the Drive folder.
4) Marissa/Ben/Camila: I'll confirm the acceptance criteria with Meridian and share the signed note in Drive — please be ready to escalate procurement items if needed.

I appreciate the team's quick turnaround on this — if we ship the MVP by next week we materially increase close probability for Q4.

Attachments: 20260924-sync-notes.docx (meeting minutes).

— Jordan
Enterprise AE | Redwood Inference
